message: Command `grep -rn "SIMDJSON_PADDING" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/simdjson/include/simdjson/ --include="*.h" | head -10 && echo "---" && grep -rn "handle_unicode_codepoint" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/simdjson/include/simdjson/ --include="*.h" | head -20` executed with exit code 0.

message.content:
Now I understand the vulnerability. `handle_unicode_codepoint` calls `hex_to_u32_nocheck(*src_ptr + 2)` which reads 4 bytes starting at `src_ptr + 2`. This is called when parsing a `\u` escape sequence. If the JSON input ends with a truncated `\u` escape (e.g., `"\u` or `"\u12`), then `src_ptr + 2` may point near the end of the buffer, and reading `src[0]` through `src[3]` could read past the end of the padded string buffer.

Let me look at where `handle_unicode_codepoint` is called and understand the padding. The simdjson library uses `padded_string` which adds SIMDJSON_PADDING bytes of padding. Let me check the padding size.
